notes:
Account snapshot: mid-market product org (customer engagement SaaS). Evaluated Hosted API for 6 week POC, now moving to Dedicated due to throughput needs and data residency. CRM notes + timeline below.

Initial discovery + priority:
- 2026-01-20 discovery call (Alex R, Jamie C, Product lead Maya Singh). High-level: embed chat assistant into CS console, doc search for knowledge base, personalization snippets in product UI.
- Primary constraints: EU + NA data residency, SSO (SAML) for internal tooling, SOC2 required. Want KMS integration for encryption-at-rest.

Hosted POC (Jan-Feb):
- POC used hosted_api with gpt-ish open model variants (customer prefers open weights but ok with Redwood-curated).
- Traffic profile: average 120 rps at peak for embeddings + chat fan-out; typical chat session 250 tokens with bursty traffic during support peaks.
- Observed: token costs under expected but 99th pctl latency spiked during peaks (~450ms). Cache reduced cost for repeat queries but not enough for peak SLOs.
- Customer quote: "Good dev DX, but we can't risk latency spikes in production. Need predictable tails."

Dedicated evaluation + demo (Feb-March):
- 2026-02-10 POC kickoff for dedicated trial (reserved pool on dev region). Setup: VPC peering, private endpoints, KMS stubbed.
- 2026-02-28 POC results: sustained throughput improved 3-4x, 95th pctl latency 180-220ms, 99th pctl ~320ms with continuous batching enabled.
- Demo (2026-03-02): walked through canary rollouts, burst behavior, console metrics (token-level cost). SE notes: KV/prefix cache gave big wins for docs.

Pricing/packaging negotiation specifics (primary topic):
- Customer prefers a 12-month reserved commit for predictable unit economics. Target ARR band ~75k-200k.
- Preferred commit structure proposed by customer: baseline capacity = 50 GPU-hours/day equivalent with monthly ramp to 100 GPU-hours/day by month 3. Need burst up to 2.5x baseline during product launches.
- Redwood proposal (initial): 12mo commit at 60 GPU-hours/day equivalent with 25% discounted burst pool (burst multiplier x2 at 50% extra fee) and overage at list price per GPU-hour.
- Customer pushback: wants clearer overage cap and burst pricing floor (no surprise bill > 30% of committed spend in any month).
- Negotiation points: ramp schedule (months 1-3), clear definition of "burst" (concurrent capacity vs. sustained hours), overage cap (suggested 30% of monthly committed spend), early-termination pro-rata rules, and buffer for holiday spikes.
- Technical ask: automatic fallback to hosted_api compatible model variants when Dedicated pool exhausted (for graceful degradation). Also require per-route SLOs and tracing hooks to map errors to routes.

Open technical/contractual items to resolve:
- Data residency clause: customer requires explicit EU-processed token logs (audit_logging + retention controls). Legal submitted DPA with redlines on 2026-03-09.
- Burst guarantee: customer wants guarantee that burst will be available up to 2x baseline for at least 8 hours during any 7-day window; Redwood needs capacity planning and pricing adjustment.
- Overage modeling: customer asked for fixed overage rate table (banded by % over commit) rather than per-hour list to simplify forecasting.

Next steps (short):

- External: send updated term sheet + sample SOW to customer by 2026-03-12 (ACTION: Alex).
- Legal: Redwood legal to respond to DPA redlines by 2026-03-16.
- SE: finalize runbook for VPC peering and KMS integration, confirm live demo of failover to hosted_api for edge-case on 2026-03-18.

- Budget cadence: procurement window opens 2026-04-01, decision expected mid-April.
